summary:
# NOTES ON TWO BOOKS (C. J. Cutcliffe Hyne)

## BOOK 1: CAPTAIN KETTLE ON THE WAR-PATH (1916, Methuen; Gutenberg 78784)
Stories with Captain Sir Owen Kettle, K.C.B. (red torpedo beard, wooden leg, Wharfedale Particular Methodists chapel, farm near Grassington/Craven, Yorkshire; wife Lady Kettle, business lady, sells Kettline/Quale's Sheep Dip-based rose mildew mixture; son-in-law/relative Arthur Hunter, grandson/boy Arthur who eats gooseberries; Horner's Perfect Cure patent medicine). Companion: Martin Carnforth, M.P. (ex-"Carnforth", gun-runner, grouse-shooter, Bradford/Yorkshire). Chapter list:

**I. The Supply Ship.** Kettle & Carnforth plan to catch a German submarine off Ireland (Carnforth: Admiralty ignored earlier tip; submarine sank 7 steamers + 4 trawlers). New Orleans: Morrissey's saloon (Canal St., French side; Morrissey's nose broken by Kettle earlier). They're drugged, shanghaied aboard tanker *Grüda* (Norwegian-owned, Chicago charter, ~1,800 tons, Captain Schlich-named Kettle alias; mate calls him "unipod"). Kettle named Olsen/Schlich; made pantryman. Submarine rendezvous; German captain; Whiteheads; a 3-inch shell explosion killed two Germans. Kettle thrown Norwegian skipper down ladder, KO'd quartermaster, rang full speed; submarine's diving rudders scraped; *Grüda* rammed over submarine; torpedo tube fired inboard → sub exploded. *Grüda* sank. Second (Dutch-style) submarine fired on Sowegian (Norwegian) starboard lifeboat, sinking it. Carnforth and Kettle righted port lifeboat, landed Irish coast; landlord Pat. Kettle asks to wire wife about keeping Quale's Sheep Dip secret.

**II. The Mine-layer.** *Grimsby Twins* (steam trawler; skipper Captain John Henry Shepherd; twins John Henry & Arthur Cleethorpes Shepherd; cat Joe with yellow melinite-stained fur; McCrae chief engineer from Edinburgh/"E'mbro'"; Olssen Third Hand (German-sympathiser, killed); old Dick, cook, fries liver sausage). Hit mine; twins killed (one headless). Shepherd prays, takes jolly boat with 7 survivors. Boards mine-layer *Bishop Argles* (ex-Tommy Argles' Lowestoft trawler), kills crew with axe; Hull Harry died, Albert Henry dead. Captain uses spare otter board to tow a mine, sinks light cruiser by mine. Olssen pushed over rail. Through mine-field in fog to Heligoland Bight; drives Bishop Argles into a battle cruiser's side, mine explodes, sinks it. Shepherd still lives in England; photograph of twins framed with 76 German helmet spikes; cat limps with one ear missing. Newspaper: Berlin claims raid, British lose 13 destroyers.

**III. Cotton.** Holly Holroyd (actor, claims ex-land-agent to Sir Berkeley Craig; "Jasper Kay in The Reptile") visits Kettle at farm (Arthur present, cheese/beer offer). Plan: stop cotton to Germany. Neutral port (unnamed; "Ballahassee" in joke); Kettle alias "Professor Owen"; Holroyd alias "Professor" trio. Holroyd: "fluxite tabloids" and "deferred ignitor" (stolen from Louvain Germans). Air-guns fire fluxite darts into cotton bales from water tower (ferro-concrete), with stork nest. Fires; German with moustache & spectacles killed. Escape across roofs. Kettle proposes cotton fires, telegram to Arthur's grandmother about curd cheesecakes. Kettle wired M.P. warning.

**IV. Gun-Runners.** Captain Image of *M'poso* (Black Funnel line, Liverpool; Purser Balgarnie; 3rd mate Price (dyed eyebrows, Welsh snoring); 4th Officer "Jones" = Kettle's alias? actually Lee-Wentworth? No—Jones is Navy officer). Abadah Colony; Acting-Governor Crawford; Commandant Craigie of Hausa Constabulary (238 men). Other Power's Colonial Secretary; Dr. Carl Josephs (butterfly man, gun-runner to African headman, Winchesters). Schmaltz (Dutch factory owner, Other Power agent) & Gebruden/Aaronstein. Navy Jones swapped cargo marks, tossed Schmaltz. Gunnery-Lt T.R.B. Lee-Wentworth on HMS *Desolation*; Other Power Colonial Secretary fell; Crawford knighted.

**V. The Intervening Wire.** Dr. Mary Brown (Norfolk, Girton, Wych Street, Brown's cocker spaniels; Mrs. Brown's begonias) hunts a German submarine in Wales bay; Kettle captures it (flat hatch wire, scoop water). Kettle deflects compass with electric wires; submarine torpedoes trawler *Ulfrida Crump*. Kettle's verse ("Huns obscene"/"Britain's Queen"). Explosive bombs; submarine surrenders; Kettle bombs his own captured sub's remaining crew. Mary wounded, Kettle drinks Horner's.

**VI. Rejoining at Once.** Lieut. John B. Plough RN (Marienbad, girl); train to Germanic port; middle-aged millinery woman from Bradford (Madame Arthur, Manningham); escape via house; stolen collier; uses coal smoke; sinks German destroyer with loco boiler. Plough drops her at Harwich.

**VII. The Lady Killer.** Grouse shooting at Cow Ghyll butts with Carnforth; Kettle shot sniper (woman; Fräulein Berta Schauer, ex-secretary of Sir Hermann Vogelheimer, baronet). Vogelheimer's heat-ray wireless. Derelict barquentine; Kettle's gun; German submarines (two) sunk; Carnforth's barrister/stockbroker die. Kettle's accordion, pulpit, Wharfedale chapel.

**VIII. An Eye for an Eye.** Western Front; Belgian Mumm (humpbacked cinematographer, drug user), wife Madame Mumm killed by Germans; Mechanics' Lodge; boiler-trolley-traction engine escape from Louvain-like town into Holland; film of German officers hanged.

**X. That Rhine Tour.** Zeppelin captured on moor; Germans locked in adit; Carnforth; Dr. Brown joins as skirt-wearing stowaway; drops bombs on Kiel canal, Zeppelin burns in Denmark. Kettle writes Rhine poems for chapel.

**X (second). The Inventor of Meltite.** S.J. Livingstone (Levenstein, Paisley-born, Bradford dyewares, enamels, Pommery '06); meltite thermite-like; partners Sir Thomas Hillcote (7th bt, motor boat *Drowning Made Easy*), ex-Lt Bell (locomotor ataxy, "Tinkle"); they sink ships; submarine takes Livingstone; he's offered earldom & £2m; ends unresolved.

## BOOK 2: HONOR OF THIEVES (1899, Fenno; Gutenberg 66637)
Chapters I–XXVI.

- I. Antecedents of Patrick Onslow: Amy Rivers (ward of Theodore Shelf; engaged to Hamilton Fairfax, shipping office clerk). Onslow: Harrow, Cambridge, diplomatic service, jilted by Mabel Kildare (married Duvernay). "The Great Traveler."
- II. Shelf (Marmaduke Rivers & Shelf, Oceanic Steam Transport Co.; Park Lane; dog George, wire-haired fox terrier). Onslow revealed Shelf was in Barcelona gambling hell (Cuatro Naciones). Plan: Everglades channel, £500,000 gold on *Port Edes*.
- III. Mrs. Laura Shelf's bank overdraft; ball extravagance; Shelf threatens murder/bankruptcy.
- IV. Ball at Latchfords'; Fairfax Kent estate purchase needs £15,000 from Amy's trust.
- V. Bimetallism: Onslow's Everglades land scheme; Shelf proposes insuring/sinking *Port Edes*; Onslow demands half.
- VI. Captain Owen Kettle (red beard; loss of *Doge of Venice*) hired; "£500" fee.
- VII. Specie loading in Liverpool; anarchist warns; coal trimmer thrown.
- VIII. Send-off: crew (Germans, Glaswegian engineers, donkeyman Sullivan Irishman).
- IX. Ground-bait: infernal machine found; Kettle's poetry (sonnets to magnolia/Cleopatra).
- X. Mutiny quelled: Kettle shoots crew man, coin toss.
- XI. To-Night: Kettle/Onslow plan explosion in forehold.
- XII. Derelicion: Onslow blows intake valve; crew abandons in two lifeboats.
- XIII. Donkeyman & Kettle partner; Onslow sees Elsie Kildare in schooner.
- XIV. Pirates' Harbor: Everglades channel; Nutt (one-eyed) & Hank (plume-hunters) take steamer.
- XV. Results in London: Port Edes lost; Fairfax quits Shelf's Brothers S.S. Association.
- XVI. Mrs. Shelf's dinner: Cabinet Minister promises baronetcy (Birthday List) for political support.
- XVII. Trust matter: Shelf forged co-trustee (Canon of Winchester) power; Fairfax demands Amy's trust funds; Shelf repays from Brothers money.
- XVIII. Plume-hunters' dinner: Hank killed by Nutt; Nutt suicide; Kettle takes steamer.
- XIX. Subjects for matrimony: Elsie Kildare, Van Liews; Kent-Williams, Robinson at Point Sebastian.
- XX. Point Sebastian: Onslow hides gold in Everglades sinkhole; cables Shelf "Right".
- XXI. Cyclone at Point Sebastian; Onslow and Elsie proposed; she refuses stolen money.
- XXII. Shelf's ball; police arrive; Shelf flees on *Gazelle*.
- XXIII. Decisions: Kettle wants farm in Canada; Onslow keeps gold secret.
- XXIV. Shelf caught at Lundy; jailed at Portland.
- XXV. Closing: Amy & Fairfax; Mrs. Shelf (Donna Laura Anaquel) in Paraguay.
- XXVI. Lucky Man: Reginald Lossing buys Port Edes claim; Kent-Williams and Lossing dig up gold in Everglades; Onslow married Elsie Kildare; Kent-Williams proposes to Mrs. Duvernay (Mabel), refused.
